slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.brief: A metal of given work function is illuminated with light of a given wavelength; ask whether emission occurs and if so, find the stopping potential via the photoelectric equation.

stem: Light of wavelength $400\ \text{nm}$ falls on a metal surface having work function $2.0\ \text{eV}$. Take $hc = 1240\ \text{eV nm}$ and $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ \text{C}$. The stopping potential is

verdicts.working: Photon energy = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV. Thus K_max = 3.1 − 2.0 = 1.1 eV, so the stopping potential is 1.1 V.

working:
Photon energy $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{1240}{400} = 3.1\ \text{eV}$. Maximum kinetic energy $K_{\text{max}} = E - \phi = 3.1 - 2.0 = 1.1\ \text{eV}$. Stopping potential $V_0 = \frac{K_{\text{max}}}{e} = 1.1\ \text{V}$.

Independent check: Photon energy = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV. Thus K_max = 3.1 − 2.0 = 1.1 eV, so the stopping potential is 1.1 V.
solution:
Photon energy is $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=\dfrac{1240}{400}=3.1\,\text{eV}$. By Einstein’s photoelectric equation,
$$K_{\max}=E-\phi=3.1-2.0=1.1\,\text{eV}.$$
Since $K_{\max}=eV_0$, the stopping potential is $V_0=1.1\,\text{V}$. Delimiter
